fields.title: Day 30 — “I Have Seen the Lord!”
fields.body_html:
“Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, ‘I have seen the Lord!’ And she told them what He had said to her.”

— John 20:18 (BSB)

After Jesus called Mary’s name, He gave her a job. He told her to go and tell His disciples that He was alive.

And Mary did. She ran to the disciples and announced, “I have seen the Lord!”

Mary Magdalene became the very first person to tell the news that Jesus had risen from the dead. The most important message in all of history, and Jesus trusted a woman to carry it first.

Think about everything Mary had been through. Before Jesus found her, she had been tormented and trapped. Then Jesus set her free. She followed Him and supported His work. She stood at His cross when others ran. She stayed at His tomb when others went home. And now she got to tell the world the best news ever.

Mary’s story is a picture of this whole book.

She faced her fear. She must have been terrified at the cross and confused at the tomb, but she stayed.

She used her voice. When Jesus told her to go, she went and told.

She served. She had supported Jesus with what she had.

She led. She carried the message to the disciples first.

And she followed Jesus, all the way.

That’s what it means to be brave. Not to never feel afraid, but to follow Jesus with your whole heart, and to tell others about Him.

Look back at everything you’ve learned in these 30 days. You learned to bring your worries to God and to trusted people. You learned to use your voice: to speak up, say no, ask for help and tell the truth in love. You met women who served with their hands and hearts. You learned to lead by going first, speaking wisely, standing firm, asking questions, serving and passing faith on. And you met the brave women who followed Jesus.

Now it’s your turn. You’ve seen the Lord in these pages. Go and tell!

A true story: Lilias Trotter was a young woman in England who could paint beautifully. One of the greatest art teachers in the country told her that if she gave herself to painting, she could become one of the greatest artists England had ever seen. But Lilias loved Jesus more than she loved fame. She laid down that bright future and sailed to Algeria, in North Africa, to tell people about Jesus. The work was slow and lonely, but she stayed for nearly forty years. And her gift wasn’t wasted: she painted beautiful little books that told the story of Jesus in ways the people could understand. She chose to be faithful instead of famous. You can read her whole story in Brave for God.

Think about it: What’s one brave thing you’ve learned in this book that you want to keep doing?

Try this: Be like Mary Magdalene. Tell someone today about something Jesus has done for you.

Dear Jesus, thank You for Mary Magdalene, who followed You all the way and told the world You are alive. Make me brave like her. Help me face my fears, use my voice, serve, lead and follow You with my whole heart. Help me tell others about You. In Your name, Amen.

fields.title: Conclusion: Brave Daughter
fields.body_html:
You made it through another 30 days! Well done, brave daughter of the King.

In Book 1, you learned who you are: loved, chosen and made on purpose by God. In this book, you learned what that means for how you live. Because you belong to God, you can be brave.

You learned that being brave doesn’t mean never being afraid. It means bringing your worries to God and to people who love you, resting at night in His care, not worrying so much about how you look, living one day at a time and remembering that His perfect love drives out fear.

You learned to use your voice like the five daughters of Zelophehad: to speak up at the right time, to say no to what’s wrong, to never keep secrets that hurt, to ask for help and to speak the truth in love.

You met women who served: Phoebe, Priscilla, Dorcas, Peter’s mother-in-law and the widow of Zarephath. And you learned to serve with gladness.

You learned to lead like Miriam and the queen of Sheba, with wise words, standing firm, serving others and passing faith on like Lois and Eunice.

And you walked with the brave women who followed Jesus: Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Susanna, the woman who touched His cloak, the mother whose faith wouldn’t quit, and the women at the cross and the tomb.

You also met five more real women who trusted God bravely: Helen Roseveare, Pandita Ramabai, Ida Scudder, Elisabeth Elliot and Lilias Trotter.

That’s a lot of brave women! And now you’re one of them.

If you haven’t trusted Jesus yet

The bravest thing you can ever do is trust Jesus with your whole life. He died on the cross to take the punishment for your sins, and He rose again, just like Mary Magdalene saw. He offers you forgiveness and a place in God’s family forever. You can pray something like this:

Dear Jesus, I believe You are the Son of God. I believe You died on the cross for my sins and rose again. I’m sorry for the wrong things I’ve done. I trust You as my Savior, and I want to follow You all the way, like the brave women who followed You. Thank You for making me a daughter of the King. Amen.

If you prayed that, tell someone: your mom or dad, a pastor, a leader or a Christian friend!

What’s next

In Book 3 of Daughters of the King, you’ll learn about growing up: your feelings and emotions, how God designed your body and the changes that come as you grow, making wise choices, discovering what God might be calling you to do, and finding women who can help you grow.

Until then, be brave. You are a daughter of the King.

“For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.”

— 2 Timothy 1:7 (BSB)
